title: Joropo llanero band
summary: Joropo is the music and dance of the great grassland plains of Venezuela and Colombia. A small band of a harp, a four-string cuatro and maracas drives a quick rolling rhythm that leans between two and three beats at once.
howToPlay: Nine lanes stand for the band: three harp bass strings, four harp melody strings, the cuatro and the maracas.
Notes travel toward a line at the bottom; strike each lane just as its note arrives.
Begin with maracas and cuatro, then let the harp bass walk in, then play the whole band.
Keep the rolling feel: every beat is split into three quick strokes.
rules: Each beat is divided into three, so strokes fall on the beat and on the two thirds that follow it.
A stroke within a hair of the note is perfect, a near one is good, and a missed one scores nothing.
An extra stroke while a song is running costs a few points.
Each song plays twice; three stars need roughly nine notes in ten on time.
The cuatro lane stands for a whole strummed chord and is sounded as one note here.
heritageNote: Joropo is kept alive in the llanos of Venezuela and Colombia by family bands, festivals and contests of singers and harpists. It is danced as a quick, stamping couple dance and sung with long improvised verses.
